sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fitness Biometric Tracking and Wellness Telemetry Apps

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 (BCBCA), particularly ss. 10 (articles), 12 (notice of articles), 14 (certificate of incorporation), 51 (share capital), 119-120 (directors), 186 (unanimous resolutions in lieu of directors' meetings), and 422 (annual report and dissolution default); supplementary forms regulation under the Business Corporations Act (Forms) Regulation, B.C. Reg. 52/2004.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (Corporate Registry), operating through the Corporate Online electronic portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application submitted via Corporate Online, comprising Notice of Articles (Form 1), Incorporation Agreement (Form 2), adopted Articles (Form 3) and Director Consent (Form 4), culminating in the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under BCBCA; a BC ULC may be incorporated with one no-par value common share subscribed for de minimis consideration (commonly CAD 1) by the sole incorporator. Additional equity or shareholder loans may be contributed post-incorporation as operational needs require.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: CONSENT RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE DIRECTOR OF [ULC NAME] (THE 'CORPORATION'), ADOPTED PURSUANT TO SECTION 186 OF THE BUSINESS CORPORATIONS ACT (BRITISH COLUMBIA). RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscriber's subscription for one common share is accepted, allotted, and issued to the sole incorporation subscriber; 2. The registered and records office at [address], Vancouver, British Columbia is adopted; 3. [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed President/Chief Executive Officer, Secretary, and Treasurer, respectively, each with signatory authority; 4. The standard ULC bylaws are adopted to the extent consistent with the Articles; 5. Officers are authorized to open banking accounts, execute banking resolutions, and complete all federal, provincial, and municipal business registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services – Corporate Online (Name Request Module)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to Corporate Online with a valid BCeID. Conduct a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) preliminary availability search, then file a Name Reservation Request for the proposed name ending with 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC'. A reserved name is held for 56 calendar days; alternatively, incorporate under a numeric name without reservation.
required_dossiers: NUANS search report (if mandatory search triggered)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused for confusing similarity, file a written reconsideration request with the Director of Corporate Registry within 30 days, or amend the proposed name and submit a new reservation request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and solicitors (pre-filing preparation; no government filing at this step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 1 (Notice of Articles) stating the ULC name, the registered and records office in British Columbia, the authorized share structure (no-par common shares), and the first director(s). Execute Form 2 (Incorporation Agreement) and adopt the statutory Articles (Form 3). Obtain each director's Form 4 (Consent to Act as Director) and verify BCBCA eligibility and residency requirements.
required_dossiers: Form 4 – Consent to Act as Director for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Perform a pre-filing internal completeness review against the BC Registry examination checklist; correct any typographical, address, or share-class inconsistencies before electronic submission to avoid requisition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation application through Corporate Online; pay the prescribed statutory filing fee by credit or debit card; receive an electronic acknowledgment and, upon approval, the Certificate of Incorporation with the official effective date. Online filings are normally examined and issued within one business day.
required_dossiers: Payment authorization for the prescribed filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry examiner issues a requisition, file corrected documents within the stated deadline; if the application is rejected, resubmit as a new application and, where applicable, claim a refund of the prior fee under the BC Registry refund policy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Charter Delivery and Share Allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and first director (corporate records administration; no government filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, prepare the statutory records folder: minute book, share register, register of directors and officers, and registered office records. Allot and issue the subscriber share certificate, ensure the Notice of Articles is certified, and deposit all charter documents at the BC registered and records office.
required_dossiers: Share subscription agreement and share certificate
Minute book and corporate records ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation or Notice of Articles contains a ministerial error, apply to the Corporate Registry for correction under the BCBCA remedial provisions; any defective share certificate should be cancelled and reissued promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Consent Resolution and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the ULC (internal corporate governance action; no government filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole director executes a unanimous consent resolution in lieu of the first board meeting under s. 186 BCBCA, covering: approval of the subscriber share subscription; adoption of the registered and records office; appointment of the President/CEO, Secretary, and Treasurer; authorization to open banking accounts; and ratification of pre-incorporation contracts. File the signed resolution in the minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed director or officer cannot serve, the board appoints a substitute under the BCBCA and the Articles, and the consent resolution and registers are updated accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax, Payroll, and WorkSafeBC Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online); BC Ministry of Finance (Provincial Tax); WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Business Number (BN) and register the ULC for GST/HST (RC18) where taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000; register for BC provincial sales tax (PST) on digital subscriptions; create the federal/provincial corporation income tax account; if hiring staff, open the payroll deductions account and register with WorkSafeBC. The ULC is treated as a taxable Canadian corporation for Canadian tax purposes; any U.S. check-the-box pass-through election is a separate U.S. tax filing.
required_dossiers: Director and officer identification (SIN or tax identification), as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects or queries the registration, reconcile entity name and Business Number discrepancies and resubmit; where registration is late, mitigation of penalties and interest may be sought through a voluntary disclosure application under the CRA Voluntary Disclosures Program before CRA contact.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Premises Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Business Licence Office (e.g., City of Vancouver); local building and fire safety authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business licence (including the home-based business designation if operating from a residence) before commencing operations; for a leased office, secure fire safety inspection, occupancy permit, and electrical and building safety clearances under the BC Building Code. Pure software and digital health app development ordinarily requires only this local operational licence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles
Lease agreement or home-based business declaration
Fire and occupancy inspection report (for leased premises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal licence is refused on zoning grounds, apply for a temporary use permit or variance, or relocate the operational and registered office and file a Notice of Change of Address with Corporate Online.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial manufacturing licensing board applies to ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 software publishing. Referential authorities: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) and the BC Ministry of Jobs, Economic Development and Innovation, Technology and Innovation Division; no industrial production permit is triggered for a fitness biometric tracking application.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no sectoral operating permit is required for pure digital software activity; the only operational licence is the municipal business licence. A Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) under the Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282, would be required only if the wellness telemetry tracker makes diagnostic or device-type claims under the Food and Drugs Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (provincial); Impact Assessment Agency of Canada / Environment and Climate Change Canada (federal)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — pure digital services business with no physical construction or manufacturing; no designated project under the Impact Assessment Act, SC 2019, c. 28, and no registration or full EIA required under the BC Environmental Assessment Act. A site-specific environmental screening is not necessary for leased office space.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero industrial discharge to air or water. The company must comply with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 for general office operations, manage electronic waste and batteries through approved provincial recycling programs, and require any cloud hosting providers to maintain ISO 14001 or equivalent environmental management certification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: WorkSafeBC registration and an occupational health and safety program are mandatory under the Workers Compensation Act once employees are engaged; municipal fire safety certification and building occupancy clearance are required for leased premises, including electrical safety certification per the BC Electrical Code and structural load compliance per the BC Building Code. For health and fitness data processing, a Privacy Impact Assessment should be completed in accordance with BC's Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) and the federal PIPEDA, with guidance from the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner for British Columbia.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); portal: CRA My Business Account and Form RC1 registration; BC sales tax administered separately by British Columbia Ministry of Finance (Consumer Taxation Branch) via BC PST registration portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The BC ULC is incorporated under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act. Upon incorporation, the CRA automatically creates a Business Number (BN, 9-digit) and corporate income tax account. For GST/HST, the ULC must open a separate BN-C (GST/HST) account by filing Form RC1 or using CRA online registration; a BC PST number must be separately obtained from the BC Consumer Taxation Branch if the ULC makes taxable sales of software or digital services in BC. Non-resident shareholders and directors of a BC ULC should verify director-residency requirements and appoint a Canadian representative/agent where required; all foreign-source ownership documentation and banking details must be kept on file to support registration and zero-rating claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian check-the-box election exists. A BC ULC is a taxable corporation under the Income Tax Act and BC tax law, subject to entity-level federal and provincial taxation. For U.S. tax purposes only, the ULC may be treated as an eligible entity under U.S. Treasury Regulation §301.7701-3 and may elect to be a pass-through/disregarded entity via Form 8832, because it has unlimited liability. Hybrid entity characterization may trigger Canadian s.94.1/GAAR or OECD hybrid mismatch analysis where payments are treated inconsistently in Canada and the United States; elections must be documented contemporaneously.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal VAT) and British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) — combined indirect tax system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable sales for GST/HST small-supplier registration; CAD 10,000 in BC taxable sales for BC PST small-seller registration. Digital supply via app stores is generally subject to these thresholds once taxable sales exceed the relevant threshold in a calendar quarter/12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or government e-invoicing APIs. CRA accepts electronic invoices/records (PDF, XML, EDI) if they are accurate, complete, and retained for six years. BC PST requires invoices or sales receipts issued to BC purchasers to state the seller's PST number and the PST amount separately where PST applies; no pre-clearance or digital stamping requirement exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GST/HST zero-rating is available on supplies of digital/intangible software exported to non-resident recipients who will use the software outside Canada, provided the supply is made to a non-resident and is not in respect of real or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of supply. Physical exports require the goods to be delivered outside Canada as soon as is reasonably possible. Zero-rating documentation must demonstrate the non-resident status of the recipient, the offshore location/use, and the arm's-length nature of the transaction. BC PST does not apply to sales of software delivered outside BC to non-resident customers.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) export documentation (for physical goods; not required for pure digital downloads)
Commercial invoice or sales contract identifying the non-resident recipient and payment terms
Bill of Lading / proof of delivery outside Canada for tangible exports
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer evidence demonstrating payment from abroad
GST/HST zero-rating supporting records: Schedule VI Part V analysis and software usage/location documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny zero-rating and reassess within the normal four-year reassessment period, or without time limit in cases of misrepresentation or fraud. False or inflated export claims attract penalties under the Excise Tax Act (including up to 25% gross-negligence penalty on the amount claimed), compound arrears interest, loss of input tax credits, and potential criminal prosecution for wilful evasion. BC PST audits may also claw back PST-exempt treatment where export evidence is insufficient, with late-payment penalties and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); currency issuance and monetary policy are governed by the Bank of Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. B-2), while prudential bank regulation is administered by OSFI under the Bank Act (S.C. 1991, c. 46); FINTRAC enforces anti-money laundering (AML) obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) as the Financial Intelligence Unit.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a freely convertible currency on both current and capital accounts; Canada imposes no general exchange control legislation, and the former Foreign Exchange Control Board regime was abolished in 1951; pursuant to the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) the legal tender is CAD, and non-resident investors may freely repatriate capital, dividends, royalties, and service fees without prior regulatory approval; the Minister of International Trade may impose limited export/import permit restrictions under the Export and Import Permits Act (EIPA) but none apply to digital health application software or biometric telemetry data streams; profit remittance hurdles are practically limited to compliance with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) withholding tax rules on dividends (Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, 25% standard, reduced to 5% for arm's-length U.S. shareholders under the Canada-U.S. Tax Treaty of 1980 as amended by the 2007 Protocol), plus provincial payroll and corporate registrations (BC Corporate Registry, WorksafeBC where employees are engaged).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion requirement; the Bank of Canada, the Treasury Board, and the Department of Finance do not mandate repatriation timelines or conversion ratios for export or services receipts; for a British Columbia ULC exporting digital health and fitness telemetry application services, all foreign currency (primarily USD) remittance inflows from Apple App Store and Google Play Billing settlement cycles may be held abroad or converted freely; prudent treasury practice dictates converting USD to CAD within 5-7 business days to mitigate FX volatility, and netting of costs is permissible; only licensing fees for exported intellectual property under the EIPA (Goods and Services Export Permit) are exempt, and there is no obligation to file a reporting declaration with Statistics Canada unless the value of exported software exceeds the annual thresholds of the Canadian International Merchandise Trade or the International Trade in Services program (threshold at C$100,000-category-specific exemption for royalty-based software fees).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account (CAD/USD Dual-Currency) + Capital Escrow Account (for parent equity injection)
Operating Account (CAD primary) + Business Credit Line cross-border USD sweep facility
Operating Account (CAD/USD) + ULC Flow-Through Treasury Structure hybrid cash management
Operating Account (CAD) + Global Banking & Markets FX forward overlay
Operating Account (CAD) with DDA sweep to money market fund

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: HSBC Bank Canada (now integrated into RBC under the 2024 acquisition)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Grandfathered Emerald / Premier corporate accounts; primarily legacy; not recommended for new ULC onboarding

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium (conditional). Legal constraints: Fintech EMIs operating in Canada (e.g., Wise Canada, Airwallex Canada, Payoneer, and Nuvei) are chartered as Money Service Businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA; they are NOT 'banks' under the Bank Act and cannot hold Canadian deposit liabilities; thus for the BC ULC they are viable as supplementary payment-pre-processing and settlement-clearing agents, but the primary operating account must remain with a Schedule I OSFI-regulated bank; cross-border EMI routing imposes mandatory 24-hour hold requirements on EFTs (Retail Payment Activities Act, effective 2024, RPSA licensing by the Bank of Canada), and each transaction must individually satisfy identity verification thresholds for the ULC's ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) if the ULC is a pass-through entity for U.S. tax purposes; foreign EMIs domiciled in the EEA (e.g., no longer accessible post-Brexit from a UK EMI) have no reciprocity with Canadian deposit insurance (CDIC) or provincial securities deposit protection, making them non-compliant as the sole treasury rail if the entity has a physical BC Nexus; practical architecture: use a tier-1 bank as anchor, and if required for acquiring sub-accounts (Google/Apple payout aggregation), use a FINTRAC-registered MSB with a valid Money Laundering branch in Vancouver or Toronto.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for the initial identification. Under the PCMLTFA and the bank's internal facing requirements, the board of directors must appear either: (A) in person at the Vancouver branch for signatory identification, or (B) via remote video verification only if the bank administers a federally sanctioned digital onboarding program under the Canadian Bankers Association (CBA) guidelines and the individual directors hold valid Canadian or U.S. government-issued photo ID. For a BC ULC where all directors are non-resident (e.g., a U.S. parent company), OSFI requires at minimum a face-to-face or notarized signature with the corporate authorization resolution physically signed and bearer-triggered; however, in practice RBC and TD will accept a remote Jumio-style video KYC if the account is opened through their 'Business Builder Online' channel, with a coprocessor also verifying the audited certificate; but for the Capital Escrow Account (client-held trust funds) physical signing will be required by two authorized directors of the Canadian ULC at a Canadian notary office or at a Canadian embassy/consulate. Prudent route: Directors physically attend an RBC Vancouver commercial center for a single 60-minute onboarding interview; carry a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation, notice of articles, ULC articles, and the BC Registry annual report extract; the interview is waived only when total aggregate account funding is less than C$25,000 and all shareholder signatories hold verified digital trust scores.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO transparency: the bank requires identification of all shareholders holding 25% or more of the ULC; under the BC Business Corporations Act (SBC 2002, c.57, s. 51) the register of members contains shareholder names but for a ULC with a U.S. parent, the ultimate shareholders are identifiable only after multiple layers of Delaware or Washington LLC cascades.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarized organizational chart evidencing the full chain from BC ULC to ultimate human beneficial owners; signed certificate from the ULC's corporate secretary confirming no one individual holds more than 25% without identification; extract of the BC registrar's transparency register (register of members) filed within 7 days; U.S. parent's certificate of good standing from Delaware/WA; if any shareholder is a trust foundation, attach a full 'know-your-trust' package including declaration of trust and settlor identification from the licensed trustee law firm; and a CIS (client identification sheet) with CRA Business Number, corporate signature, and director's birth date with passport scan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident lender negative control: the ULC is 100% owned by a U.S. corporation (pass-through); the branch may classify the deal as a high-risk 'foreign national control' requiring enhanced due diligence if the U.S. parent is newly incorporated (under 1 year) or lacks audited financial statements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare six months of pro-forma financial projections (P&L, cash flow, balance sheet) with a CPA-review engagement letter; signed subscription agreement from the U.S. parent committing equity injection of at least 30% of the account's anticipated annual flow; complete AML questionnaire (bank-issued form) demonstrating that the ULC's fitness tracker app has no FinTech payment processing of third-party funds; current CRA Notices of Assessment for the ULC (if any) and the U.S. parent's federal EIN; the ultimate U.S. shareholder's personal net-worth statement or a letter from a U.S. CPA attesting to the parent's solvency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk sourcing of funds: initial equity contribution from a U.S. parent via a digital bank (e.g., Mercury or Brex) raises OFAC/PCMLTFA flags because the routing bank may not be a recognized SWIFT member (Mercury uses a partner bank, Evolve Bank & Trust).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a chain-of-origin wire confirmation from the underlying partner bank (Evolve Bank & Trust) showing the ABA routing; include the U.S. parent's formation certificate, operating agreement, and a written 'declaration of source of wealth' signed by the CEO and CFO; the ULC must provide its own bank statement showing that no intermingled third-party flows exist; include legal fee invoices from the BC incorporation counsel evidencing that the equity was used solely for incorporation and pre-launch technology licensing; if the capital is injected via a Delaware LLC, include its W-9, EIN, and a certificate of incumbency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-adjacent user geography: the fitness app is available globally and may be downloaded in jurisdictions subject to UN/Canada sanctions (e.g., Russia, Iran, North Korea, Crimea, Venezuela) through Apple and Google app stores; however, the bank may consider the ULC to have 'indirect sanctions exposure' because the settlement account receives gross app store revenue regardless of end-user jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Obtain from Apple App Store and Google Play Billing a formal letter each confirming geo-blocking of sanctioned territories for the app's distribution; include the app's privacy policy and certified localization disclaimer prohibiting downloads/residency from sanctioned jurisdictions; the ULC must add a treasury protocol: within 24 hours of receiving aggregated store revenues at the Canadian settlement account, execute a negative media/OFAC screening of the counterparty Apple/Google entities (both are listed on OFAC's non-SDN menu but are permitted parties); sign a written declaration that the ULC does not directly or indirectly onboard users requiring money transmission and that no Iranian/Russian payment processors are used; deliver third-party AML/CTF consultant report confirming the revenue stream originates solely from platform solutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual asset / crypto contamination: the fitness app offers a 'digital wellness token' in the pipeline; a ULC with an unlimited liability structure may be viewed by the bank as a vehicle for mask-passing crypto proceeds if any in-app purchase is convertible to a crypto-backed stored value.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The ULC must formally abandon or reschedule any digital token launch; provide the corporate board resolution declaring that in-app purchases are exclusively fiat-based via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, with no external wallet, no crypto payout, and no use of distributed ledger rails; the policy must be embedded in the accounting manual and audited; attach a FINTRAC MSB registration certificate if the ULC ever holds virtual currency wallets (it should not); obtain a legal opinion from Canadian counsel confirming that the revenue stream is 'digital goods' not 'virtual currency' under the PCMLTFA definition of Virtual Currency (s. 2(1) and FINTRAC Guidance 9/2023).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the initial equity injection (U.S. parent to BC ULC): use the U.S. parent's Schedule I bank (e.g., JPMorgan or Bank of America) to initiate a USD SWIFT MT103 wire to the ULC's RBC Canadian Dollar account via the RBC New York branch (SWIFT: ROYCCAT2), with the payment purpose code 'GIFTCAPINJ' - equivalent to a direct investment; for Canadian regulatory purposes the instruction must include: (i) the ULC's corporate CRA Business Number (BN) and BC registration number; (ii) the remitter's full name and account number; (iii) in the 70-line: 'Equity injection under BC Business Corporations Act; no consideration; no loan; ULC shares issued to parent'; (iv) add the standard International Trade in Services/Investment remittance code 'B-EQUITY-100' as per the Bank of Canada's Canadian Balance of Payments classifications; banks will perform an OSFI anti-money-laundering value-check on any wire exceeding C$100,000; provide the wire confirmation from the parent, an authorized board resolution signed by two directors referencing the exact amount and account number, and the ULC's share subscription agreement to preempt a 72-hour compliance hold; alternative rail: use the Bank of Canada's Lynx real-time gross settlement system (LVTS successor) only for same-day CAD high-value transfers between domestic institutions; a U.S. parent may also use a Canadian clearinghouse electronic funds transfer (EFT) for amounts under C$25,000, but the SWIFT MT103 is the only fully compliant rail for cross-border equity injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for outbound business trade settlements of the BC ULC: (1) Operational disbursements (marketing campaigns, sub-processor fees, and licensing payments to vendors in the U.S., Ireland, or Singapore): SWIFT MT103 with corresponding 'OUTGOING' instruction, referencing the invoice number, currency (USD or CAD), and purpose code 'TRADE-SERVICES' (Bank of Canada 'IMM-11' classification for international trade in services); (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) are permissible but not needed for a digital-health services model; however, for app-development subcontracting to an offshore engineering vendor (e.g., India or Eastern Europe), the standard routing is a documentary collection or irrevocable LC (ICC UCP600) issued by the ULC's domestic bank in favor of the offshore vendor, with the ULC's operating account providing clean reimbursement; the bank will require an underlying software development agreement, a pro-forma invoice, and a work-statement to fulfill the 'invoiceless' disbursement rule; (3) for royalty payments to a U.S. parent (IP license), the outbound rail must include a NOTICE TO THE CRA under Part XIII: the bank is not the withholding agent, but the ULC must effect the withholding via the CRA's electronic remittance (or pay-at-source) using Form NR4 or T2-S13; international clearing rails: SWIFT gpi (Global Payments Innovation) is strongly recommended to reduce transit time to 30 minutes for SDGL (Same-Day Global Low value) transactions; SWIFT MT103 is the only accepted message type for Trade Finance clearing, whereas MT202 COV must be used for cover-through correspondent bank clearing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward (deliverable) - CAD/USD: OTC with a Canadian Schedule I bank (RBC, TD, BMO), available for a ULC with audited financial statements or a bank credit line; standard tenor 1M-18M; a 10% collateral margin required for unrated ULC; ISDA Master Agreement (2010) or local Canadian Master Agreement with a supporting Credit Support Annex (CSA) if not clearing through the Canadian Derivatives Clearing Corporation (CDCC).

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF): permitted in Canada for CAD crosses only where the counterparty offshore jurisdiction has capital controls (e.g., exotic currency conversion); for CAD/USD, NDFs are disallowed if the underlying flow is FX deliverable; NDF may be layered for hedging the ULC's CNY-denominated Chinese App Store settlement flows (Apple/Google aggregate China payouts) where only an offshore CNY NDF is executable; executed via RBC Capital Markets or TD Securities under a non-cleared margin rules exemption (certainty exemption for commercial hedgers).

Cross-Currency Swap (CAD/USD principal exchange): a plain-vanilla cross-currency interest rate swap between the BC ULC operating cash flows and a U.S. parent debt service; applicable only when the ULC holds a bilateral loan from the U.S. parent and wants to swap floating-rate USD liabilities into fixed-rate CAD; typical minimum notional C$20 million; empowered by CDCC rules or QFC stay rules; not relevant for a pre-revenue or early-stage ULC (excess cost), but incorporated into the treasury roof for future scale.

Flexible-Forward (window forward): contract allowing the ULC to execute in partial amounts within a forward window (e.g., monthly app-store settlement sweeps), maximizing hedging precision of variable-volume USD/CAD passive income; requires corporate treasury policy approval signed by secretary; available at BMO and RBC without central clearing if the counterparty risk is capped at ULC net asset value.

Zero-Cost Collar (long put/short call coupon-neutral): moderately permissible instrument for a ULC where the Canadian entity has a stable USD revenue history from Apple/Google payout; must be executed under the pre-clearance of the ULC Board and a senior secured inter-creditor agreement with the bank; physically or cash-settled at expiry, ensuring that any equity-marking gain is taxable as eligible capital gain; the structure prevents a forward mark-to-market liability exceeding the ULC's paid-up capital.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (with confirmation of Individual with Significant Control register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of incorporation; filing accepted within 2 months after the anniversary date without penalty
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fee imposed if filed after the two-month window; administrative strike-off and dissolution after one year of continuous non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of an auditor unless unanimously waived by shareholders; a shareholder holding at least 5% of issued shares may require an audit. No revenue-based statutory threshold for a private non-distributing ULC.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for reporting issuers; ASPE (Canadian Private Enterprise GAAP) for non-reporting private ULCs

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BCBCA Part 9.1 requires an Individual with Significant Control (ISC) register; the annual report must state that the ISC register is accurate and complete, and each shareholder must confirm their ISC status upon filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individual with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 4,000–10,000 (USD 2,900–7,400) per audit engagement if required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined (15% federal Part I general rate + 12% British Columbia general corporate income tax rate). The ULC is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) because it is controlled by a non-resident parent, so neither the federal small business (9%) nor the BC small business (2%) rate applies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED Investment Tax Credit: 15% non-refundable on qualifying Canadian R&D labour and expenditures. British Columbia Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit: 17.5% refundable on qualifying BC salary and wages attributable to interactive digital media products (fitness app qualifies if the product has meaningful interactive functionality and the corporate permanent establishment is in BC). The effective rate on eligible development labour can be reduced by up to approximately 4.7 percentage points where both credits are captured.
